common_name: Thunderhead Sedum (Extra-Sturdy Deep Rose-Red Upright Stonecrop)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Thunderhead's unusually thick, dark stems stay upright without staking even after heavy rain.

directions: Thunderhead was bred to correct the single biggest complaint about older tall sedums: floppy stems that split open under heavy flower heads or a summer downpour. Its stems are noticeably thicker and more rigid than Autumn Joy or Matrona, holding the huge, domed clusters of deep rose-red flowers perfectly upright from late summer into fall. Foliage is blue-green and glaucous through the growing season, giving good textural contrast well before bloom. Grow in lean, well-drained soil in full sun, since rich or overly moist conditions undercut the cultivar's structural advantage; established plants shrug off drought and heat and need dividing only every four or five years.
sources: Chicago Botanic Garden Plant Evaluation Notes

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in average to lean, well-drained soil in full sun; avoid rich, wet ground, which weakens stems on this and other showy stonecrops.

directions: Iceberg is a white-flowered sport of the pink-blooming showy stonecrop group, opening pure white, flat-topped flower clusters in late summer above pale, blue-green succulent foliage. The cool white color reads as a fresh, clean accent among the more common rose and mauve border sedums, and it ages to a soft parchment-tan rather than the brick tones of pink cultivars, giving a different winter silhouette. Grow in lean to average, sharply drained soil in full sun; like other upright stonecrops it is prone to splitting open at the crown in fertile, moist conditions. Divide every three to four years in spring once the clump becomes congested or begins flowering less densely at the center.

common_name: Coral Reef Sedum (Coral-Pink Flowered Blue-Green Sunsparkler Stonecrop)

planting.note: Set divisions in spring in gritty, well-drained soil in full sun; the mounding habit fills in fastest when not crowded by taller neighbors.

directions: Coral Reef carries smooth, powdery blue-green foliage on a tidy mounding plant, a cooler-toned counterpart to the burgundy- and chocolate-leaved members of the Sunsparkler series. In late summer it produces abundant clusters of soft coral-pink flowers that stand out clearly against the blue foliage rather than blending into a dark leaf backdrop the way some series members do. Plant in gritty, fast-draining soil in full sun, where the foliage color stays truest and the habit remains dense rather than open. It works well at the front of a sunny border or spilling over a low wall, and rarely needs division more often than every four to five years.
sources: Proven Winners Sunsparkler Sedum series information

common_name: Dream Dazzler Sedum (Cream-and-Pink Variegated Sunsparkler Stonecrop)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; variegation is strongest in full sun and can green up somewhat in shadier spots.

directions: Dream Dazzler stands out among the Sunsparkler cultivars for its variegated foliage: cream-white leaf margins surround gray-green centers, and the margins flush soft pink as temperatures cool in fall, giving the plant three-season interest well before bloom. Bright pink flower clusters open in late summer above the variegated mat, drawing bees and butterflies. Grow in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun, since strong light keeps both the variegation and the pink foliage blush at their best; shade tends to mute the leaf pattern. The low, spreading habit suits rock gardens, container edges, and the front of a sunny border, and it needs division only when the center of the mat begins to thin.
sources: Proven Winners Sunsparkler Sedum series information

common_name: Parker's Variety Yarrow (Classic Tall Golden Fernleaf Yarrow)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring in lean, well-drained soil; stake in exposed sites, since the tall flowering stems can lean under wind or heavy rain.

directions: Parker's Variety is one of the older, longer-established golden fernleaf yarrow selections, predating many of today's filipendulina cultivars and still valued for its exceptionally large, flat mustard-gold flower heads held on strong, tall stems above ferny gray-green foliage. It is a workhorse cut-flower and dried-flower plant, since the broad flower heads hold their color for months once cut and hung to dry. Plant in lean, very well-drained soil in full sun; overly rich or wet ground produces taller, weaker stems prone to flopping. Established clumps are extremely drought- and heat-tolerant, and dividing every two to three years in spring keeps flowering strong and flower heads at full size.

common_name: Lachsschönheit Yarrow (Salmon Beauty Yarrow, Classic German Hybrid)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in lean, very well-drained soil in full sun; this German-bred hybrid needs excellent drainage and struggles in heavy, wet clay through humid summers.

directions: Lachsschönheit (German for 'salmon beauty') is a classic Achillea millefolium hybrid from the same mid-20th-century German breeding line that produced 'Fanal' and 'Paprika', bearing flat clusters of warm salmon-pink flowers that soften to a paler blush as they age, above finely dissected, aromatic gray-green foliage. The muted salmon tone blends easily with both hot colors and pastels in a mixed border, making it a versatile filler among yarrow cultivars that tend toward pure red, yellow, or white. Plant in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun, since rich or soggy ground weakens stems and invites crown rot. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigorous, upright flowering.
sources: general horticultural reference on German Achillea millefolium hybrids

common_name: Apple Blossom Yarrow (Soft Pink Heirloom Cottage Yarrow)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, surface-sowing since yarrow seed needs light to germinate, or plant divisions in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Apple Blossom is an older, widely grown cottage-garden yarrow cultivar bearing flat clusters of soft, pale pink flowers with a slightly deeper pink center, a gentler, more pastel effect than the vivid cerise of 'Cerise Queen' or the saturated tones of the patented Seduction series. The finely cut, aromatic gray-green foliage forms a low mat beneath taller flowering stems from early summer into fall. Plant in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; rich or consistently damp soil leads to weak, flopping stems and a shorter bloom season. It tolerates poor soil, heat, and drought once established, and dividing overgrown clumps every two to three years keeps the planting tidy and floriferous.

common_name: Red Velvet Yarrow (Compact Non-Fading Deep Red Yarrow)

planting.note: Set out divisions or container plants in spring once soil has warmed, in lean, very well-drained soil in full sun.

directions: Red Velvet was bred to hold a deep, saturated red flower color through the whole bloom season rather than fading to dusty rose or salmon the way many older red and pink yarrow cultivars do, giving flat-topped clusters that read as true red from midsummer into fall. Its compact, well-branched habit stays more upright than taller heirloom red selections, reducing the need for staking in open sites. Plant in lean, fast-draining soil in full sun; wet or overly fertile ground quickly causes floppy stems and crown rot, especially in humid regions. Deadhead spent clusters to extend bloom, and divide crowded clumps every two to three years in spring to keep the planting vigorous.
